history.summary: TOWN CORRECTION: CSV lists 'Mysore' but the famous temple stands in Srirangapatna, Mandya district, ~13-16 km from Mysuru. Per ASI, an inscription records its construction in 894 CE by Tirumalaiah, a Western Ganga vassal, over an older shrine (local accounts attribute the inner sanctum to 817 CE donor Hambi). Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana granted the village as an agraharam to Ramanujacharya in the early 12th century; a Veera Ballala II inscription (1210 CE) records additions; the entrance tower is Vijayanagara in style, with Wodeyar-era contributions. Held in esteem by Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan; ASI-protected monument of national importance and one of the Pancharanga Kshetras (Adi Ranga).

name: Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple
town_description: Srirangapatna is an island town on the Kaveri river in Mandya district, the former de-facto capital of the Mysore kingdom under Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan, and a major Vaishnavite pilgrimage centre.

travel.airport: Mysuru Airport (~25 km); Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru (~150 km)
travel.railway: Srirangapatna railway station (~500 m, directly behind the temple complex)
travel.road: ~16 km from Mysuru via NH-275; well connected by KSRTC buses

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; weekdays to avoid crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: 7:00 AM-1:30 PM and 4:00 PM-8:30 PM daily; entry free, special darshan Rs. 250
